claims.value: light: 'A549 [S.aureus-HG001 ]<GFPpos-infected|GFPneg-exposed|mock-infected> <t>h p.i. <infection|control> experiment <n>'; heavy: 'A549 heavy SILAC global standard (13C6-Arg/13C6-Lys) aliquot spiked into <light source name>'
claims.evidence: One raw file per sorted sample (54 runs). Raw names encode the sorted population (gfppos / gfpneg), time point (1_5h..6_5h) and experiment batch (111214 no BR tag; 120505 *_BR4; 120626 *_BR5 for the infection experiments; 120505_OV4_KRIS_HPI_<n>_<t>_BR1..BR3 for controls). README.txt maps the control runs HPI_<n>_<t>_BR1/BR2/BR3 to A549_control_sorted_SILAC_BR1/BR2/BR3. It maps the infection batches 111214 / *_BR4 / *_BR5 to the gfp_pos and gfp_neg tables BR1 / BR2 / BR3. Each light source is one physical sorted-cell sample. The heavy standard is one "global SILAC standard" (Data Brief Fig. 1 legend) spiked into every sample (Data Brief 2.5: "Infected, exposed, and control host cells were spiked with equal numbers of SILAC standard A549 cells"). Its rows name the standard and the aliquot, one aliquot per sample/run. A single shared heavy source name is refused by sdrf-tools build, because each aliquot is a separate one-file row with the same biological replicate, technical replicate and fraction.

claims.location: comment[label] rows 1-108 (odd rows SILAC light, even rows SILAC heavy)
claims.value: SILAC light = sorted study sample; SILAC heavy = heavy A549 standard
claims.evidence: Channel map, explicit: PRIDE sample protocol "sorted infected and non-infected host cells ... spiked 1:1 with untreated A549 cells grown in medium containing 30 ug/mL 13C heavy isotope labeled arginine and 70 ug/mL lysine. The heavy isotope labeled A549 cells served as internal standard"; Data Brief 2.5 "Infected and mock-infected A549 cells cultured in eMEM with 12C arginine and 12C lysine were subjected to cell sorting. Heavy-isotope labeled A549 cells ... were collected as spike-in standard for all groups". Checked against the deposited tables: Elucidator xls report per-condition Intensity1/Intensity2 and Ratio columns of SILAC pairs (e.g. TLN1 1_5_h_inf_BR1 Intensity1 7111.6 vs Intensity2 31914.8) with heavy peptides annotated K[134.115] / R[162.1211] (+6.02 Da on K and R). Multiplicity 2 (light + heavy) confirmed; no third channel exists. Direction of biology is not used for the map.

Heavy channel is the spiked-in internal standard against which every sample ratio is computed (PRIDE: "Ratios of the host proteins were calculated between the samples (control, GFP-positive or GFP-negative) and the heavy labeled standard"). PRIDE:0000899 reference (OLS, not obsolete), same encoding as campaign super-SILAC precedents PXD009766 / PXD002669.

PRIDE organisms NEWT:9606; Cellosaurus CVCL_0023 OX NCBI_TaxID=9606; NCBITaxon:9606. Host-cell dataset only: PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol and Data Brief 2.7 say the host search used a SwissProt database restricted to human proteins (the S. aureus proteome is deposited separately in PXD002384).
Cellosaurus CVCL_0023 "Derived from site: In situ; Lung; UBERON=UBERON_0002048"; UBERON:0002048 lung.

PRIDE sampleAttributes/organismParts CL:0000066 epithelial cell; Data Brief "human alveolar epithelial A549 cells". CL:0000066 (not obsolete). The more specific type II pneumocyte is not asserted (only cited as a property in the 1976 reference title).

Cellosaurus CVCL_0023 DI NCIt C3512 Lung adenocarcinoma; MONDO:0005061 lung adenocarcinoma (OLS). This is the disease of the cell-line donor; S. aureus infection is encoded separately in characteristics[infection status] / [infectious agent].
All samples are cultured A549 cells (Data Brief 2.2).
Cellosaurus CVCL_0023 "Population: Caucasian" -> HANCESTRO:0005 European ancestry (batch rule 9).
Cellosaurus CVCL_0023 AG 58Y.
Cellosaurus CVCL_0023 SX Male.
Donor age 58Y (>= 20Y, batch rule 9); EFO:0001272 adult.
All cells derive from the single A549 donor (Cellosaurus CVCL_0023).
Paper/PRIDE "A549 cells"; EFO:0001086 label A549 (Cellosaurus DR EFO_0001086); not obsolete.
Cellosaurus AC CVCL_0023, OX 9606 (human), so no cross-species name collision.
Cellosaurus ID A-549.

Data Brief 2.2: A549 cultured in eukaryotic minimal essential medium "eMEM, 1x MEM without arginine and lysine" + 4% FCS + 12C Arg/Lys (light) or 13C Arg/Lys (heavy standard, "in equal concentrations in the respective SILAC eMEM"). OLS NCIT search for "minimum essential medium" returned no term, so the stated name is written (validator ontology warning expected).

claims.value: light rows: 1..3 within each (factor value[infection status], factor value[sampling time]) group; heavy reference rows: 1 (one global standard)
claims.evidence: Data Brief 2.3: "Three different internalization assays were performed with each three independent biological replicates" (n = 3 per group, Specifications table). Infected/exposed: experiment 1 = 111214 runs, 2 = 120505 *_BR4 runs, 3 = 120626 *_BR5 runs (three separate infection dates) = gfp tables BR1/BR2/BR3 per README.txt. Controls: 1/2/3 = raw tags BR1/BR2/BR3 = control_sorted_SILAC_BR1/BR2/BR3 per README.txt. Every group holds replicates 1, 2, 3, one per independent internalization assay (spec README.adoc:330, batch rule 3). The mock controls were their own internalization assay ("(iii) as negative control"), so they are numbered separately from the infection experiments. All heavy reference rows have 1. The Data Brief describes a single "global SILAC standard" collected "as spike-in standard for all groups": one standard material, aliquoted. Its 54 aliquots are technical splits, not biological replicates (campaign precedents PXD003316, PXD005854).

claims.value: GFP-positive infected / GFP-negative exposed / mock-infected (light); not infected (heavy standard)
claims.evidence: README.txt maps the gfppos/gfpneg runs to the A549_gfp_pos/gfp_neg_sorted tables and the HPI_<n>_<t>_BR1..3 runs to the A549_control_sorted tables. Raw names gfppos / gfpneg = GFP-positive (infected, contains internalised GFP-expressing S. aureus) and GFP-negative (exposed, no internalised bacteria) sorted host cells (PRIDE/Data Brief cell-sorting text). Control runs (120505_OV4_KRIS_HPI_<n>_<t>_BR1..3) = mock-infected A549 cells "mock-infected with sterile infection mix containing pMEM ... subjected to cell sorting applying the same settings" (Data Brief 2.3/2.5). Heavy standard = "untreated A549 cells" (PRIDE). Custom characteristics column (spec Extending Templates; campaign precedent PXD014577 characteristics[infection status]).

claims.value: Staphylococcus aureus (GFP-positive infected and GFP-negative exposed rows); not applicable (mock-infected, heavy standard)
claims.evidence: Infection with S. aureus HG001 pMV158GFP at MOI 25 for 1 h, then lysostaphin (Data Brief 2.3). NCBITaxon:1280 Staphylococcus aureus (OLS, not obsolete). HG001 has no own NCBITaxon node; NCBITaxon:93061 (NCTC 8325) is the parent lineage used for the bacterial search database, not the strain, so the species is written and the strain goes to characteristics[infectious agent strain]. Exposed cells shared the culture well with bacteria but carried none internally; the agent column records exposure to the pathogen, the status column records internalisation.
Data Brief 2.1: "S. aureus HG001 [2] carrying plasmid pMV158GFP [3] for continuous production of GFP"; raw names RN1HG / HG001. Custom column, free text.

claims.location: characteristics[sampling time] rows 1-108; factor value[sampling time] rows 1-108
claims.evidence: Time post infection from raw names (<h>_5h = <h>.5 h p.i.); PRIDE/Data Brief "collected hourly between 1.5 h and 6.5 h after infection". The two names *_6_6h_gfpneg* (111214 and BR4) are written 6.5 hour: the design is hourly 1.5-6.5 h, their gfppos partners in the same batch are 6_5h, and BR5 names the same sample 6_5h_gfpneg; README.txt maps both 6_6h files to the gfp_neg BR1/BR2 tables, whose six conditions are 1_5_h..6_5_h_inf_neg_BRn (no 6.6 h condition). The heavy standard is not a time-point sample.

claims.evidence: PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol / Data Brief 2.7: "Carbamidomethylation of Cys was a fixed modification only in the human search. Oxidation of Met and SILAC labeling of Arg and Lys (6.02 Da) were variable modifications". +6.02 Da = 13C6 (Data Brief: heavy "13C" arginine/lysine; PRIDE identifiedPTMStrings MOD:00544 6x(13)C labeled residue); xls modified sequences K[134.115] (128.095+6.02) and R[162.1211] (156.101+6.02), C[160.0302] carbamidomethyl. UNIMOD:188 Label:13C(6) for both residues (batch rule 11, MT=Variable). Search engine: SEQUEST 3.5 in Rosetta Elucidator, human SwissProt 2012. README.txt maps all 54 runs to a search output.

claims.evidence: README.txt maps raw IDs 68 (HPI_1_1_5h_BR1) and 75 (HPI_8_1_5h_BR2) to the search outputs A549_control_sorted_SILAC_BR1_{peptides,proteins}.xls (IDs 77/86) and ..._BR2_... claims.value: v1.1.0; ms-proteomics v1.2.0, human v1.1.0, cell-lines v1.1.0; NT=sdrf-skills;VV=v0.1.0; proteomic profiling by mass spectrometry
claims.evidence: Batch rules 1 and 10; templates fit the samples (human cell line, MS). clinical-metadata/oncology-metadata not declared: commercial cell line, no patient samples (batch rule 15).

limitations: Control identity and the experiment-to-table mapping are stated in the deposit, not inferred. README.txt MAPPINGS assign the 18 runs HPI_<n>_<t>_BR1/BR2/BR3 to the A549_control_sorted_SILAC_BR1/BR2/BR3 tables. They assign the infection batches 111214 / 120505 *_BR4 / 120626 *_BR5 to the gfp_pos/gfp_neg tables BR1 / BR2 / BR3. Run names remain the only per-file label of the condition, because the raw headers carry no sample description.

The 1.5 h conditions of control experiments 1 and 2 (runs HPI_1_1_5h_BR1, HPI_8_1_5h_BR2) were searched (README.txt mapping) but are absent from the exported control BR1/BR2 tables. This is consistent with the protocol excluding 1.5 h host data after the search. The two runs are annotated like all the others.

Two raw names say 6_6h (111214 and BR4 gfpneg); they are annotated as 6.5 hour (see claim). Three raw names carry an _r suffix (presumably re-injections). Only one file per sample is deposited, so technical replicate is 1 throughout.

Heavy standard: one "global SILAC standard", with biological replicate 1 on all reference rows. The deposit does not document whether the standard was one harvest for all three infection and three control assays, or was prepared per assay. Each reference row has its own aliquot source name, because sdrf-tools build refuses one shared source name with identical biological replicate, technical replicate and fraction across single-file runs.
Precursor and fragment mass tolerances of the SEQUEST search are not reported (not available), so parse_sdrf convert-openms is expected to fail on them.

The companion research article (Surmann et al. J Proteomics 2015, PMID 26244908) is not open access and was not read. Design details come from the PRIDE protocols, README.txt and the open-access Data Brief (PMC5063755), which describes the same experiment.
The 111214 raw header read was reset by the server. Instrument and method were read from three other runs, and they agree with PRIDE and the paper.
characteristics[culture medium] = Minimum Essential Medium has no NCIT term (OLS search empty), so it is written as stated.

S. aureus proteins: PRIDE and the Data Brief say the host search database was human-only, so no pathogen proteome is declared in this SDRF. The bacterial proteome is deposited separately as PXD002384, a different dataset and not a duplicate.
